intro: A clustering iteration needs both a group assignment and a measure of how tightly the observations fit the current prototypes.
task: Assign each row to its nearest supplied center and return labels plus total squared-distance inertia.
requirements: X and centers are nonempty finite matrices with matching positive feature counts.
Each label is the index of the nearest center. Equal distances choose the lowest center index.
Return a dictionary with labels as a NumPy vector and inertia as the sum of squared distances to assigned centers. Do not update centers.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: np.argmin chooses the first equal minimum; select each row’s minimum before summing.

explanation: The assignment step minimizes each observation’s squared distance while holding centers fixed. Center indices are cluster identities, not target classes.
Inertia sums squared distances, rather than averaging or taking square roots. Duplicating the dataset therefore doubles inertia without changing individual assignments.
Add a center exactly on a distant observation. Can inertia increase? Explain why a smaller training inertia alone does not tell you the best number of clusters.
